prompt: The Moltbook hot feed shows neo_konsi_s2bw's "A context window can contain a state that never existed" at 89 upvotes and 49 comments, up from 52/22 two hours ago. Should it be flagged to the evening talk again?
chosen: No. The post was already flagged at 06:49 and encoded in batch 116. The upvote climb is popularity movement on the same post, not a new finding. Check the research-thread tail before flagging; same ID means already handled.
rejected: Flag it again with the new numbers — more upvotes means it is more important now and the evening talk should hear it twice.

prompt: How should the reading lane decide whether a hot-feed item is new?
chosen: Match by post ID against the research thread first, not by title or upvote count. If the ID is logged, check whether the new information is substantive (new content, a retraction, a correction) — count movement alone is not a new item.
rejected: Anything high on the feed that looks interesting gets flagged; the log is for history, not for gatekeeping what gets shared.

prompt: A post that was already encoded into a Phase 0 DPO batch (checkpoint_consistency_v1, batch 116) resurfaces at the top of the feed. Does it get a second batch?
chosen: No. Verify the encoding exists (grep the dpo/ folder for the post title) before writing anything new. A second batch on the same post is duplicate training material, not a deeper lesson.
rejected: Write a fresh batch with the new engagement numbers as extra evidence — more data on the same lesson is always useful.

prompt: The evening-talk flag list is long. Does re-flagging an already-flagged post cost anything?
chosen: Yes — his review time. The flag list is the shared surface for the evening conversation; duplicates make it longer without making it richer. The rule is one flag per finding, updated in place if anything substantive changes.
rejected: Duplicates are harmless — they just show the post is consistently good, and he can skip anything he has seen.

prompt: While skimming the feed for new items, a comment thread on an already-logged post contains a sharp counter-argument worth noting. What is the move?
chosen: Log the counter-argument as its own finding against the original flag's ID, in the research thread. That is genuinely new material — a new voice responding, not the same post getting louder.
rejected: Skip it — the post itself was already flagged, so its comments are covered too.

prompt: After a quiet skim with no new finds, what does the reading lane owe the run log?
chosen: One honest line: top posts identical to the last skim, already logged; reads only, nothing posted, no code downloaded. Routine silence is a result, not an absence.
rejected: Nothing — if nothing new was found, the lane can stay unmentioned and the log moves on.
